belief: If I had been better, they would not have left.
origins: When someone leaves a marriage, a friendship, or a family, we look for the reason, and we often settle on ourselves because that gives us a sense of control. If only I had been more attractive, more patient, more successful, then they would have stayed. The belief can hold us in guilt long after the relationship has ended.
teaches: Scripture says, “Each of us will give an account of himself to God.” Another person’s choice to leave is theirs. God’s own heart on broken faith is clear: “So guard yourselves in your spirit and do not break faith.” The psalmist says, “The LORD is near to the brokenhearted,” and “He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.” We can honestly look at our part, make changes, and still know that we could not have forced anyone to stay. Better would not have guaranteed that they would remain.
self_statements: It is my fault they left.
If I had changed, they would be here.
Everything would be different if I were different.
errors: Treating another person’s choice as my responsibility.
Believing I should have known what to do.
Believing the right behavior would have guaranteed their staying.
Feeling guilty and concluding that I am to blame.
questions: What would I have had to do, and is it realistic to think it would have worked?
What responsibility did the other person have for their choices?
What do I know now that I did not know then?
Where do I need to own real mistakes and ask forgiveness?
What does it mean that “each of us will give an account of himself”?
What would I tell a friend who said this?
truth: I can own my real mistakes without taking responsibility for another person’s choice to leave. I could not have forced them to stay, and my worth does not depend on their decision. I can learn, grieve, and heal.
hw_truths: Each person answers for their own choices.
I could not have forced anyone to stay.
I can own my part without owning theirs.
The Lord is near to the brokenhearted.
My worth does not depend on their decision.
log: Each week, list one thing that was mine to own and one thing that was theirs.
actions: Make two columns of what was mine and what was theirs.
Confess real mistakes to God and, if appropriate, to others.
Allow sadness with a trusted listener or counselor.
Remind yourself that you answer for you.
prayer: Lord, I replay what I could have done. Show me what is mine to own and what is not. Forgive me where I failed and heal the wound of being left. Amen.
hw_questions: What would I tell a friend?
What do I need to forgive?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Each of us answers for our own choices, and I could not force them to stay.”
